card.name: Preparing and giving IV or inhaled doses
card.fires_on: Small words, spaces or digits inside instructions for diluting, reconstituting or infusing a drug, just before the diluent or route is named. Also partway through words like formoterol or peristaltic in administration text.

modes.label: Before the diluent
modes.description: A space, 'in', 'with' or a digit right before a diluent such as 0.9% sodium chloride or 5% dextrose.
modes.example: Dilute the contents of one vial of Angiotensin II Injection in<< >>0.9

modes.label: Before the route or device
modes.description: A linking word before 'intravenous infusion' or the equipment used to give it.
modes.example: Angiotensin II Injection must be administered as<< an>> intravenous infusion.

modes.label: Inside route-related words
modes.description: Partway through a drug or device word in administration instructions.

card.writes: It seems to favor non-oral, injection or infusion wording and to suppress 'oral' and 'orally'.
card.plain: It fires in dilution and infusion instructions, just before the fluid or route is named.
